title: Ignoring the back rank
description: A position from a real Lichess game. Black is about to make a mistake.
prompt: Black just played 26...Qa1. You are White: how do you punish it?
hints: The black king on g8 has no escape square.
Which check on the back rank can't be answered?

notes.26...Qa1: The mistake: the black king on g8 has no escape square.
notes.27.Qc8#: White goes for the back rank.

explanation: After 26...Qa1 the black king was stuck on its back rank, and White mated there. Before you move a piece that guards your back rank, check whether a rook or queen could give a check your king can't escape — and give it an escape square in time.

title: Missing a threat: checkmate
description: A position from a real Lichess game. White is about to make a mistake.
prompt: White just played 15.e3. You are Black: how do you punish it?
hints: Your opponent just ignored something you were threatening. What was it?
Look for checks and captures first.

notes.15.e3: The mistake: White plays on as if nothing were threatened.

explanation: Before 15.e3, Black was already threatening Qxf2#. White ignored it, Black carried out the threat, and it ends in checkmate. Before every move, ask: what does my opponent threaten right now?

title: Grabbing a poisoned pawn

hints: Black just grabbed a pawn. What did that cost?
Look for checks, captures and threats.

notes.29...Qxd4: The mistake: Black grabs the pawn on d4.
